## The effects of the publish or perish culture on publications in the field of educational administration in Türkiye
Aysel Çakir<sup>a,*</sup>, Dilan Kuyurtar<sup>b</sup>, Aydın Balyer<sup>c</sup>
- <sup>a</sup> Bağlarbaşı m, Sakızağacı sk, No:26/10 Maltepe, İstanbul, Turkiye - <sup>b</sup> Emek m, Şermin sk, No: 13 Darıca Science and Art Center, Darıca, Kocaeli, Turkiye - <sup>c</sup> Yıldız Technical University Educational Administration Department, Davutpaşa Kampüsü, Esenler, İstanbul, Turkiye
#### ARTICLE INFO
# Keywords: Publish or perish Educational administration Bibliometric analysis SSCI Publishing
#### ABSTRACT
This study aims to reveal the effects of publish or perish culture, which is a product of the marketization of science, in the field of educational administration in Türkiye. For this purpose, a bibliometric analysis of 253 publications written in the field of education management in Türkiye, included in the SSCI index in the Web of Science database, was performed. The distribution of publications by years, type of publication, and the subjects they focus on were examined, and at the same time, the journals published were evaluated according to their impact factors, rankings, and whether they were paid or not. As a result of the analysis, it has been revealed that the effects of the publish or perish culture on the field of educational administration are parallel to its effects on other fields.
#### 1. Introduction
Academic publishing is facing an increasingly untenable situation with the publish-or-perish rallying cry, and there is no denying the emotional and mental pressure on those who produce in this budding crisis environment (Fernandez- Patron & Hardy, 2017). As it is seen in the 'publish or perish' slogan itself, it is clear that those who want to get promoted in academia and consolidate their careers have no choice but to publish to survive (Génova & De la Vara, 2019).
This concept is quite common in higher education institutions around the world (Amutuhaire, 2022) because the increasing competition in educational institutions due to the neoliberal education policies leads to a quantitative competition among academicians in higher education institutions (Olssen, 2021). In an environment of increasing scientific competition and pressure, there has been an explosion in scientific publishing in recent decades (Grimes et al., 2018). Even though academic publications are expected to represent scientific productivity and talent (Bornmann & Mutz, 2015), the credibility of publications has not increased at the same rate as the output has increased significantly.
The effectiveness of science depends on the publication of research, which serves as a source of new knowledge. At this point, the criterion that makes a scientific publication valuable is that it is published in qualified and important journals (Atılgan, 2005). However, the number
of citations is also important. Acar and Bektaş (2021) found that only 51.34% of the papers published in Türkiye in the period 2010–2014 were cited. Based on this data, it can be said that the quantity of studies published in the mentioned period is not an indicator of scientific progress.
Another issue that does not attract much attention, but is important, is the retraction of published articles after a while. It will be important to evaluate the data on the retraction of publications that appear to be a mistake or an unethical situation to understand the contribution of academic publishing to scientific development. Kocyigit and Akyol (2022) examined retracted articles in the field of biomedicine in Türkiye and concluded that the reasons for retraction between 2000 and 2022 were plagiarism and duplication rather than errors.
There are a large number of studies on publish or perish culture in both national and international literature, and these studies mostly focus on academics views on the pressure felt on academic publishing (Balyer & Tabancali, 2023; Cole, 2000; Miller et al., 2011; Van Dalen & Henkens, 2012). There are also conceptual (Bello, Azubuike, & Akande, 2023; Frederick, 2020) and systematic analysis (Davies & Felappi, 2017; McGrail et al., 2006) studies that focus on the beneficial and harmful effects of publish or perish on the teaching-research dilemma. Considering that existing studies focus on contexts such as the academic pressure created by the publish or perish culture in a general perspective

#### *1.1.* *The publish or perish dilemma *
The characteristics that distinguish the knowledge produced by the scientific method from other types of knowledge are objectivity, completeness, verification, simple explanation, empiricism, and probabilistic thinking ([Balcı, 2008](#page-7-0)). When these features are analyzed, it is concluded that the information obtained as a result of research or experiment in a field should be a part of the knowledge in the field with the common opinions of scientists in the field. This brings us to the conclusion that a field must be institutionalized to become a science. The institutionalization of a field depends not only on the existence of departments in universities but also on the creation of organizations to pool knowledge and transfer the activities of scientists to each other. For this, scientific journals have an important place in the institutionalization of science [(Balcı, 2008](#page-7-0); [Demir, 2018;](#page-7-0) Ertas¸ & [Kozak, 2020;](#page-7-0) [Gas](#page-7-0)[paryan et al., 2016;](#page-7-0)[ Lawrence, 2008)](#page-8-0).
[Gasparyan et al. (2016) ](#page-7-0)state that the first scientific journal was the Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society, which began to be published in 1665, and that scientific papers were sent by mail. With more than 350 years of history, scientific publishing today is very different from the Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society. Today, quantitative evaluations have become more important than the content of scientific articles (Adler & [Harzing, 2009;](#page-7-0) [Gasparyan et al., ](#page-7-0) [2016)](#page-7-0). The biggest impact of the growing importance of quantitative evaluation is that it brought the slogan to publish or perish to academia. Publish or Perish is more than a slogan, it reflects a culture in academia. This culture started in the 1960s. First in the US, then in the UK, as it was considered a necessity to increase the intellectual activity of academics in business and management education (Derond & [Miller, 2005](#page-7-0); [Çıtak, ](#page-7-0) [2022)](#page-7-0) publish or perish has become a race against time for academics today (Derond & [Miller, 2005](#page-7-0); [Kaygusuz, 2012)](#page-8-0). It can be said that the biggest factor in this is the orientation of academia worldwide. To understand this orientation, it is necessary to look at the characteristics of the neoliberal era.
#### *1.2.* *A brief look at the effects of neoliberalism on publishing *
With the neoliberal era that began in the 1970s, as public expenditures were cut, academia, like almost every other field, became subject to market conditions ([Akıs¸, 2020](#page-7-0);[ Ugurlu, ](#page-8-0)˘ 2015). As a result, the criteria for academic success began to be expressed in the language of the market: competition, prestige, entrepreneurship, and performance ([Akıs¸, 2020,](#page-7-0) p. 355). Due to the effort to monopolize commercialized knowledge, knowledge also became centralized. Therefore, international institutions emerged to oversee and even direct academic production. The most influential of these institutions are databases where scientific journals are evaluated and ranked. In major databases such as Web of Science (WoS), Scopus, and Google Scholar, journals and articles are evaluated using quantitative criteria. These institutions, which are companies themselves, shape scientific production in various ways (Dogan, ˘ Dyhı & [Al, 2018](#page-7-0)). For example, WoS, the database that the Council of Higher Education (CoHE) values most in academic incentives, decided to expand regionally due to commercial concerns and quickly accepted many journals from Türkiye. Over time, performance criteria in higher education in Türkiye have changed according to international standards. Scoring is done based on the criteria set for the appointment of doctoral faculty members, associate professors, and professors at a university. According to the scoring table determined by CoHE, scoring for academic articles is as follows: Full research articles (excluding letters to the editor, abstracts, reviews, technical notes, and book reviews), articles published in journals within the scope of SCI, SCI-E, SSCI, or
AHCI receive 25 points in Q1, 20 points in Q2, 15 points in Q3, and 12 points in Q4.
The most important bibliographic criteria determining the prestige of journals are citation indexes and impact factors. The priority for academics is to publish in prestigious journals. However, the fact that a journal has a high impact factor does not necessarily mean it is more scientific (Adler & [Harzing, 2009](#page-7-0); [Beall, 2018; Demir, 2018](#page-7-0);[ Gasparyan ](#page-7-0) [et al., 2016](#page-7-0);[ Çıtak, 2022](#page-7-0)). Similarly, academics are ranked based on their h-index scores. The h-index is a measurement determined by the number of papers published and the number of citations received by a scientist or a research group. An h-index is necessary to receive various awards, incentives, and permanent employment. To achieve this, a scientist needs not only to produce influential papers but also to publish a large number of articles. These rapid changes are observed to occur by increasing the number of publications in a short period.
At this point, it is crucial to address the issue of predatory journals. Predatory journals are publications with dubious scientific value that charge fees for publishing articles. In countries like Türkiye, Nigeria, and India, the fear of job loss and the obligation to publish force academics to contribute to predatory journals [(Demir, 2018](#page-7-0)). When academics in developing countries face financial difficulties and the imperative to publish immediately to avoid falling behind in support ([Lawrence, ](#page-8-0) [2008)](#page-8-0), this tendency increases towards turning to predatory journals. The number of predatory journals blacklisted by Beall in 2016 increased from 18 in 2011 to 923 in 2016 [(Gasparyan et al., 2016)](#page-7-0). Although the Council of Higher Education (CoHE) has published the Beall List and warns academics about journals on this list, it does not consider journals in the Q4 category that charge fees as predatory if they are affiliated with a foundation.
In countries with advanced and substantial scientific knowledge, scientific activities can progress independently of external conditions like market. However, in countries like Türkiye, higher education tends to adapt more quickly to international regulations, and efforts are made to comply with rules set in place rather than adopting a critical perspective.
#### *1.3.* *Educational administration in Türkiye *
The field of educational administration finds its historical origins in the early 1800s ([Balcı, 2008)](#page-7-0); however, it can be contended that its emergence as a systematic discipline occurred during the latter part of the 19th century, characterized by the notable contributions of William Payne through his pedagogical discourse on school administration at the esteemed University of Michigan [(Hyung, 2001; Takmak, 2019](#page-8-0)). During the 1950s, the field of educational administration experienced a transformative phenomenon known as the Theory Movement [(Hyung, 2001](#page-8-0)), which was substantially influenced by the prevailing positivist paradigm (English, 2002). This movement witnessed a significant shift in scholarly attention, as researchers and practitioners directed their focus toward exploring and implementing Frederick.
Taylor's concepts of effectiveness and efficiency within educational contexts. Consequently, the studies conducted during this period were primarily concerned with establishing frameworks and strategies aimed at optimizing the performance and productivity of schools [(Takmak, ](#page-8-0) [2019)](#page-8-0). Although these studies faced critical scrutiny in the following years, prompting scholars to raise concerns about the limited scope and potential unintended consequences of an overemphasis on effectiveness and efficiency in educational administration [(Hyung, 2001](#page-8-0)), they undoubtedly contributed greatly to the institutionalization of the field.
In the latter half of the 20th century, there was a notable surge in criticism towards endeavors aimed at the technicalization and standardization of school management. This criticism prompted a significant diversification in the epistemological and methodological foundations of the field of educational administration, as scholars embraced approaches commonly characterized as post-positivism [(Takmak, 2019](#page-8-0)). This intellectual shift brought forth a range of alternative perspectives
and research methods that departed from the positivist tradition, fostering a more nuanced and multifaceted understanding of educational administration.
The inception of the field of educational administration in Türkiye is widely acknowledged to have commenced in the 1960s, primarily attributed to the scholarly contributions of Prof. Dr. Ziya Bursalıoglu ˘ and Prof. Dr. Mahmut Adem ([Yılmaz, 2018)](#page-8-0). The onset of education at Ankara University Faculty of Education marks a significant milestone in the scientization process of the field of educational administration in Türkiye [(Balcı, 2008](#page-7-0)). [Balcı et al. (2009) ](#page-7-0)assert that the process of professionalization in the field of educational administration in Türkiye, which began in the 1960s, is still in its nascent stages, and the developmental trajectory of educational administration in Türkiye differs from that of advanced countries. The progress of the field in advanced countries has been relatively slow, whereas, in Türkiye, there has been a relatively rapid advancement [(Balcı, 2008](#page-7-0);[ Turan et al., 2014)](#page-8-0).
Studies in the field of educational administration in Türkiye, as in other countries, often lack originality and creativity; studies are repetitive and simplistic [(Balcı et al., 2009](#page-7-0)). Problems arise in terms of representativeness, sample selection, and the quality of data collection tools. Especially in recent years, qualitative research has gained importance and the use of single or mixed research designs has increased in Türkiye ([Balcı, 2008)](#page-7-0). Despite having a history of approximately 80 years in Türkiye, the field of educational administration has a limited number of studies dedicated to its examination [(Yılmaz, 2018](#page-8-0)). This suggests a relative dearth of scholarly attention and research endeavors directed toward exploring the intricacies, challenges, and developments within the field. The scarcity of studies on educational administration in Türkiye indicates a knowledge gap in comprehending the distinctive context, challenges, and practices that influence the administrative aspects of education [(Turan et al., 2014](#page-8-0)). The field of educational administration is characterized by a predominance of studies that prioritize the replication and control of existing knowledge, leading to a lack of originality and this can be attributed, in part, to the career advancement pressures faced by academics in the field ([Yılmaz, 2018](#page-8-0)). Consequently, research endeavors in educational administration often gravitate towards popular subjects, driven by the pursuit of academic promotion.
The limited number of studies on educational administration in Türkiye, coupled with the prevalent "publish or perish" culture, highlights the necessity for increased scholarly engagement and research output to address the knowledge gap and advance educational policy, practice, and decision-making in the field. Although there are many studies on the 'publish or perish' motto in the Western world, this issue has gained importance in Türkiye in recent years and there has been an increase in the number of studies on the subject. To measure the impact of the motto publish or perish on the field of education management, publications in this field should be subjected to bibliometric analysis. Bibliometric analysis is one of the methods that has attracted attention in recent years. There are some studies in which educational publications examine with bibliometric analysis [(Gülmez et al., 2021;](#page-8-0) [Selçuk ](#page-8-0) [et al., 2014)](#page-8-0). [Gümüs¸ et al. (2019),](#page-8-0) analyzed the improvement of educational management and leadership in Türkiye. For this aim, they analyzed only the articles that were published on the WoS database and used scientific mapping and they focused on articles published in the most prestigious journals.
#### *1.4.* *Purpose of the research *
The main purpose of the current study is to analyze the impact of the 'publish or perish' culture on the publication process in the field of educational administration in Türkiye. Within this scholarly context, our study aims to provide an overview of the state of Turkish research published in internationally indexed journals, specifically focusing on those included in the Web of Science: Social Sciences Citation Index (SSCI). Through employing basic bibliometric analyses, we also aim to
answer the following questions:
- What is the distribution of related publications by year, author, and affiliation? - How do the published journals distribute according to their impact factors, ranking, and whether they are paid or not? - What are the citation rankings of the authors of the relevant publications? - How is the distribution of the topics cited in the publications?
#### **2.** **Method **
#### *2.1.* *Design of the study *
The study employed a bibliometric analysis method to analyze the data, which in its simplest sense is a statistical and quantitative description of the literature and the literature here means that only relevant documents whose specific characteristics can be identified (e.g. subject matter, document format, language, country of publication, etc.) are treated as a group (Nicholas & Ritchie, 1978 as cited in [Broadus, ](#page-7-0) [1987)](#page-7-0). It is considered a very useful and practical method for analyzing large bibliographic datasets (Ramos-Rodrígue & [Ruíz-Navarro, 2004](#page-8-0)). Bibliometric analysis examines the social and structural connections between various research elements such as authors, countries, institutions, and topics to provide a summary of the bibliometric and intellectual framework of a particular field [(Donthu et al., 2021)](#page-7-0). The choice of utilizing bibliometric analysis was driven in this study by the desire to uncover the emerging patterns in research components within the educational administration field, as well as to investigate the intellectual structure of the field. In addition to its role in scientific mapping, bibliometric analysis serves another crucial purpose known as performance analysis, which involves evaluating the research and publication performance of individuals and institutions (Zupic & [Cater, ](#page-8-0)ˇ 2014). In this study, the analysis of performance encompassed an examination of pertinent data extracted from the WoS (Web of Science) database, encompassing variables including the publication year, authorship, affiliated institution, journal characteristics (e.g., impact factor and ranking), citation count, and bibliographic information of the accessed articles.
#### *2.2.* *Data collection procedure *
To retrieve relevant scholarly data, a search query was executed in the Web of Science database using the following terms in the subject title field: "educational administration" OR "educational leadership" OR "educational supervision" OR "educational economics" OR "educational finance" OR "educational planning". The reason why this method was chosen is that the field of educational administration in Türkiye traditionally encompasses educational administration, inspection, planning, and economics, and also leadership is the most important topic in the field.
The country of focus for this investigation was Türkiye, thereby Türkiye was selected. Subsequently, a systematic search within the Web of Science database was conducted, resulting in the identification of a total of 276 studies about educational research within the education category. No restrictions were imposed concerning the publication year or language of the studies. It should be noted that the 276 documents were not subjected to any exclusion based on their type. Acknowledging that scientific production extends beyond research articles alone, an endeavor was made to comprehensively examine the general characteristics of publications relevant to Türkiye in this context.
To this end, 276 articles were analyzed. The boundaries of the field of educational administration in Türkiye are not fully defined. Moreover, recognizing the potential inclination of academics to submit their publications to journals across various disciplines due to the imperative of publishing, an inclusive approach was adopted by scrutinizing articles
encompassing multiple categories within the Web of Science database, in addition to the Education category specifically focusing on educational research. As a result of this examination, 12 articles that were deemed unrelated to educational administration were excluded from the subsequent analysis, ensuring a more refined and relevant dataset for the study. Furthermore, to maintain a focus on academic contributions and account for potential variations in research motivations and pressures, articles authored by non-academic teachers affiliated with the Ministry of National Education (MoNE) were also excluded from the analysis. As the investigation primarily aimed to assess the publication pressures experienced by academics, it was deemed appropriate to restrict the study to scholarly works produced exclusively by academic authors. Consequently, a total of 11 publications authored by nonacademic individuals were identified and subsequently excluded from the analysis. Taking these exclusions into account, a total of 23 articles were deemed unsuitable for inclusion in the analysis.
The data collection steps are shown below.
*Description: *Total documents retrieved using the WoS database (n = 276)
*Screening: *Documents excluded due to category, author not being an academic (n = 23)
*Relevance: *Documents assessed for appropriateness (n = 253)
*Included: *Documents included in the analysis (n = 253)
The 253 studies were transferred to an Excel table using the WoS system. On May 13, 2023, the data collection process ended.
#### *2.3.* *Analysis of the data *
After the search in the WoS database, the data related to the articles obtained were transferred to an excel file. This was done by selecting the excel format from the export command in WoS. The data in the excel file was examined by two other authors and it was decided that it met the inclusion criteria. Only the Number of Publications and Citations by Year graph was taken from the Analyze Result pane in WoS, the other graphs were created using the excel file.
A separate excel file was prepared for the data on the paid status of the journals after a search on their websites. The findings are presented in the next section.
#### *2.4.* *Findings *
Accordingly, 253 articles in the sample were analyzed according to the year of publication, authors, and the journal in which they were published. At the same time, information on the most published author and universities was also included. In addition, analyses such as journal impact factor, and author citation information are also included in this section.
#### *2.5.* *Distribution of the studies by publication years *
The number of studies in the field of educational administration published in journals included in the Social Science Citation Index reviewed in the Web of Science database is 253 in total. Numerical data on publications are presented in Fig. 1.
When the distribution by years is analyzed, it is seen that there is no general increase or decrease. The fluctuations in the number of publications can be evaluated as the fact that the productions in the field of educational administration do not have a standard or continuity. The WoS search is not restricted by year. Therefore, the first article meeting the inclusion criteria is dated 2005.
#### *2.6.* *Distribution of the document types *
The analysis of document types revealed that the majority of studies conducted in the field of educational administration in Türkiye consisted primarily of research articles. it becomes evident that out of the total 253 studies, a majority of 238 studies are classified as articles. Conversely, there is a notably lower representation of other study types, such as editorial materials, proceeding papers, review articles and book reviews. This observation may be attributed to the fact that articles carry more weight in the evaluation criteria for academic promotions. To facilitate comparative analysis, a search was conducted within the Web of Science database using the search terms employed in this study, resulting in the identification of 25 different document types. Notably, certain document types such as letters, book chapters, and discussions were not found in the studies conducted within the context of Türkiye. This discrepancy highlights the prevalence and emphasis placed on article-based publications within the academic landscape in Türkiye.

The majority of the 55 journals analyzed according to Fig. 4 are in the Q4 category. Although the distribution of the four categories was not equal, the results were close to each other. It can be said that a special weight is not given to the top-ranking journals in Türkiye. However, it is necessary to consider the number of articles. In Fig. 4, the quartile distribution of the journals according to the number of articles is given.
When the number of articles according to 55 journals is examined in Fig. 4, it is seen that 57% of the publications are in the journals in the Q4 category. Of the 56 reviewed journals, 35 charge a publication fee. In addition to the journals that charge a fee only when printed in color, some journals charge fees of up to 3000 pounds. Parallel to the marketization of science, paid publishing is increasing all over the world. The distribution of 253 studies examined in this study according to paid publication status is given in Fig. 5.
When Fig. 5 is examined, it is seen that 63% of the publications are published in journals that do not charge a fee. 95 of the reviewed studies were published in paid journals. Fig. 6 shows the distribution of these 95 studies by Q category.
When Fig. 6 is examined, it is seen that 40% of the paid publications are in Q4 and 35% are in Q3 journals. The fact that 40% of the examined publications were published in paid Q4 journals is a result of the impact of quantitative evaluations on the field before the scientific quality of the studies.
#### *2.10.* *Citation analysis *
Another indicator of performance analysis through the bibliometric method is citation analysis.[ Fig. 7](#page-6-0) shows the number of publications and citations by year.
When [Fig. 7 ](#page-6-0)is examined, it is seen that although the number of publications increases, the number of citations received does not increase at the same rate. This situation shows that the quality of studies in the field of educational administration in Türkiye has increased.

#### **3.** **Discussion and conclusion **
When the findings regarding the publication dates of the studies are analyzed, it can be said that the increasing number of academic publications in the 2000s (Gu & [Blackmore, 2016](#page-8-0)) has progressed in the same way for academic studies in the field of educational administration. During the first decade of the 2000s, the average number of academic publications in SSCI journals related to educational administration is less than 10. However, it can be observed that although there have been fluctuations from time to time, the number of publications has gradually increased since 2010. However, the reason for the fluctuation may be the removal of some Turkish journals from the SSCI index since 2012 ([Gülmez et al., 2021](#page-8-0)).
The study contains a similar output of bringing the publish or perish culture to educational administration with other fields. All areas of fluctuation, which have spread to be published according to years, are seen (Akçigit ˘ & [Ozcan-Tok, ](#page-7-0)¨ 2020). This situation is related to the acceptance and removal of the WoS archives of the journals addressing Türkiye as their basis. When WoS decided to expand its scope, the number of journals accepted from Türkiye was written all at once. This situation gives the impression that there is an increase in productivity in Türkiye. While the sample and viewers who look at the decrease in the number of publications are evaluated as superior, the fact that the mechanism that measures the productivity of the manager has been
taken over by a big computer, which emerged as a result of the marketization of science and monopolizes scientific publishing, and makes a profit for these larges is ignored.
When the types of publications were analyzed in the study, it was found that the most common type of publication in the SSCI index was research articles. Other types of production such as review articles, book reviews and proceedings are negligible. The reason for this is that the Council of Higher Education gives the most weight to article production in academic incentives and promotions. Articles are so important or other types of publications are so scarce that even bibliometric analyses are often based on articles alone. Scientific progress in a field is not just about a research paper. Activities such as congresses and reviewing books written in the field are essential for the epistemological development of the field, with scholars working collectively and discussing and examining field-specific questions. As can be seen, the publish or perish culture limits academic activities in educational administration, as in other fields, to writing research articles.
When the academicians and universities with the highest number of publications are examined, it is seen that the number of publications of co-authored studies and even international collaborations is higher. This result is in agreement with other studies (Akçigit ˘ & [Ozcan-Tok, ](#page-7-0)¨ 2020; [Gülmez et al., 2021](#page-8-0); [Lawrence, 2008](#page-8-0)). Publish or perish culture can be said to increase co-authored studies. Although this situation is accepted as positive, it is not sufficient to evaluate the quality of the production. In the study, it was observed that the ordering according to the number of publications changed when the number of citations was taken into account.
When the journals published are examined, it is seen that the majority of the articles are generally in the lower ranking journals. Qualified scientific production is a risky endeavor that requires time and serious effort. Unexpected results can be obtained in research, and these results can take the academician to very different places in the production of knowledge. The researcher has assumptions at the beginning and seeks information accordingly. However, he does not know from the beginning what will happen in the end. However, since the publish-orperish culture imposes rapid and highly cited publications, academics tend to publish according to the general trends in the field and to do 'easy' research in this respect, for which they know or predict the outcome. In addition, since there is a high demand for high-quality journals that are accepted in the field, it is necessary to wait a long time to get answers from them. It does not allow waiting in the 'publish or perish' world.
In addition to this, it has been revealed that there is a great interest in journals addressed to Türkiye. This is an indication that the field of educational administration remains at the local level. This result is compatible with various bibliometric analysis results (Acar & Bektaş, 2021; Doğan, Dyhı & Al, 2018; Ertaş & Kozak, 2020; Gümüş et al., 2019; Gülmez et al., 2021). The concentration of publications in a limited number of journals implies a certain level of preference and recognition accorded to these specific outlets within the field of educational administration in Türkiye. This finding underscores the importance placed on disseminating research within the domestic scholarly ecosystem and the significance assigned to the reputation and visibility of these journals within the academic community.
As a result of the publish or perish culture is the emergence of predator journals, one of the questions our study sought to answer was about predatory journals. As a result of the analysis, it was revealed that 40% of the publications made by paying money were in the journals in the Q4 category. It is not easy to identify which of these journals are predatory journals. Academics may not know whether the journal they send their publications to is a predator. Whether a journal is a predator or not is understood over time as the articles it publishes are seen. A journal can be considered a predator and removed from the indexes, then after a while re-entered.
In addition to predator journals, journals in the Q1 category may also charge a fee for publication. Demanding high wages is an indication that the academician is making a profit on their labor. In an environment where science is marketed, academicians have to pay money to have their quality studies published to advance in their careers and gain prestige. In low-income countries, the income of academics is also low. In this case, they have to find various incentives
To meet the high wages. It is difficult to say that academics who have to receive incentives from both the government and private institutions can produce freely.
When we look at the issues related to the publications in the field of educational administration, the prominent topics are mainly leadership and job satisfaction. The field of educational administration should be in a close relationship with many disciplines such as economics, planning, politics, social theory, and sociology. However, there are very few productions on these subjects in international publications from Türkiye. It can be said that this situation poses a threat to the future of the field of educational administration.
#### 3.1. Suggestions
It is not easy to protect the publishing adventure in the field of educational administration in Türkiye from the negative effects of the publish-or-perish culture. The end of these pressures surrounding academics will be possible through the joint efforts of academics. We recommend that academics increase their communication and interaction with each other regarding their research, focus on the information a research reveals rather than which journal it is published in, and strive to create an academic culture that enables this.
We think that this problem can be overcome when discussions on how this can be achieved are carried out by academics and when research is conducted using more diverse perspectives and different methods on publication printing.
